comparisons.explanation: Expedited deadlines and procurement design versus deliberate evasion.

queries.text: What does GAO and each agency actually attribute?
queries.status: answered from retained audit; no motive investigation

answers: Army/ICE officials cite leadership deadlines and failed ICE procurements. Army cites speed, innovation and price; ICE contracting staff criticize absent review and LPTA. Defense disputes balance; GAO attributes decisions to both agencies. This does not establish a secret motive.

comparisons.explanation: Spare capacity may serve separation, isolation and surge needs.
answers: ICE cited these functions. GAO observed subdividable units and invoices for unneeded meals. DHS describes short-stay staging near an air hub. No measured safe usable capacity follows from either gross beds or occupancy.

comparisons.explanation: Open recommendations may coexist with corrective work or administrative closure lag.
answers: One recreation yard opened but remained inadequate in September; contract replaced; Army milestones documented. Historical table excludes later fixes. No item-level reinspection establishes current correction.

comparisons.explanation: An acceptable overall inspection and a replacement vendor could indicate improvement without proving closure.
answers: February inspection still found49 deficiencies and3 priority issues. April replacement was too early to evaluate in GAO audit. Same dated requirement-specific evidence standard would apply to any operator.

comparisons.explanation: Pricing failure can be tested separately from medical correction.
answers: C02 pp7–8 documents absent cost-saving measures as of August2026, despite March replacement award. This is later dated evidence, not merely an inference from recommendation Open status. It does not resolve the safety residual.
